We hit an odd issue this morning when our AP team tried to accept the supplier invite inside the customer portal where we integrated Redwood's embedded SDK. - Tried toggling third-party cookie settings (some corporate browsers block 3rd-party cookies)

Thanks for the flag and the traces — good set of artifacts. Quick notes from triage: 

1) Repro and immediate cause- we reproduced locally by loading the invite flow via our embeddable iframe. The IdP SAML response is issued, but the Redwood session cookie is being set from an iframe context. Modern browsers with default privacy settings will reject cookies set without SameSite=None; Secure, and some corporate policies block third-party cookies entirely. In that case the post-auth redirect ends up in the iframe without a persistent session and the UI shows a blank frame.

2) Why full tab works- when opened in a new tab the session cookie is set in a first-party context and everything completes normally.

3) Short-term workarounds (fastest to implement)
- Ask Saffron's IT to open the invite link in a new tab (manual but reliable).
- Instruct them to enable third-party cookies for the customer portal domain (policy change on corporate devices).

4) Medium-term fix (engineering change)
- Update the embeddable SDK to use a small pop-up / top-level redirect for the final auth handshake (post-SAML). That avoids setting session cookies inside an iframe. Implementation estimate: 3 dev-days + QA + deploy. We can ship a targeted minor version with the change.

5) Security notes- We checked CSP headers: our iframe is allowed by frame-ancestors for the portal, and IdP assertions look fine. No auth tokens leaked in the trace.

Plan proposal: ship pop-up/redirect auth in SDK, and while we work it the CS team should provide the two short-term mitigations to the customer. Rafael – can you size infra changes (if any) and slot this for a minor sdk release?

Ben Carter
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
